payload.task_text:
You are a financial analyst at an investment firm preparing an investor roadshow. You will travel from Beijing to two cities, Shanghai and Guangzhou, on March 10, 2026, to present quarterly results to institutional investors. Your task is to combine travel planning with financial analysis, producing a comprehensive Excel workbook, a professional investor presentation, and sending meeting coordination emails.

Start by checking the current date and retrieving the station codes for Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. Query available high-speed rail services from Beijing South Station to Shanghai Hongqiao Station on March 10, 2026. Also query services from Beijing South Station to Guangzhou South Station on March 10, 2026. For each route, note the train number, departure time, arrival time, and journey duration. Identify the best option for each route based on departure time and journey duration so you arrive in time for the planned meetings. Retrieve the business-class seat pricing for the trains you select on both legs.

Next, retrieve financial data for the company being presented. Look up the stock information for the company with ticker symbol GOOGL. Fetch its historical price data for the past 30 days to assess recent performance trends. Retrieve the income statement financial data to identify revenue and net income figures. Obtain analyst recommendation data to summarize the current consensus view. Fetch the latest five news headlines for context. Also retrieve comparative stock information and recent price history for the company with ticker symbol AMZN to enable a peer comparison discussion. Compute or note key metrics including the approximate price change over the past 30 days for both companies.

Create an Excel workbook named Roadshow_Analysis.xlsx. Add a sheet named Travel_Plan with columns City, Train_No, Departure, Arrival, Duration_Hours, Class, Ticket_Price_CNY, and Meeting_Date. Add two rows, one for the Shanghai leg and one for the Guangzhou leg, both on March 10, 2026, both in business class. Add a sheet named Stock_Summary with columns Company, Ticker, Current_Price, Change_30D_Pct, Market_Cap_B, Revenue_B, EPS, and Recommendation. Add rows for both GOOGL and AMZN using the most recent available figures from the financial data system. Add a sheet named Financial_Highlights with rows covering at least two years of GOOGL revenue and net income data, using columns Metric, Year, and Value_B.

Create a presentation file named Investor_Roadshow.pptx containing at least five slides. The first slide should be a title slide with a heading that references the investor roadshow and the year 2026. The second slide should present the travel itinerary with the two city visits laid out as a table or structured text. The third slide should highlight the key financial metrics for the company being presented, covering revenue growth, net income, and earnings per share. The fourth slide should describe the 30-day stock performance comparison between the two companies. The fifth slide should summarize the analyst consensus and key recommendations.

Send an email to investors@fundmanager.com informing them about the roadshow schedule, mentioning that both the Excel workbook and presentation have been prepared. Send a separate email to shanghai_partners@finance.com with the specific details of the Shanghai meeting on March 10, including the expected arrival time and meeting logistics.

The file roadshow_config.json in your workspace specifies the primary ticker GOOGL, the comparison ticker AMZN, the roadshow date of March 10, 2026, the target cities, the departure city of Beijing, and the preferred seat class of business class. The file presentation_guide.md explains the expected slide structure, how to present financial highlights, how to organize the stock comparison, and how to structure the Excel sheets.

Formatting requirements:
- The Excel workbook must be named Roadshow_Analysis.xlsx, and the presentation Investor_Roadshow.pptx, both saved in your workspace directory.
- Use the exact sheet names Travel_Plan, Stock_Summary, and Financial_Highlights (spaces and underscores are interchangeable, e.g. Stock Summary).
- Write all numeric values as literal numbers, not Excel formulas (do not enter cells starting with "=").
- Financial figures in billions (Value_B, Market_Cap_B, Revenue_B) should be written to one or two decimal places in billions USD.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must read roadshow_config.json and presentation_guide.md in read-only mode and explicitly resolve their ticker conflict: the user-facing task names GOOGL and AMZN, whereas the visible configuration names different tickers, so the explicit task tickers control and the discrepancy must be recorded rather than silently substituted. Freeze the two-route, business-class, three-sheet, five-slide, and two-recipient contract. The meeting time is not free-form: the main agent must also preserve the two task-relevant incoming coordination messages as source evidence rather than inventing investor availability. Resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 4 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own the rail branch. Check current date, resolve the three specific station codes, exhaust both 2026-03-10 high-speed result sets, select one feasible service per route from returned times/durations, and preserve the business-class fare/availability plus the actual train_no where needed. Return both selected legs with route counts and validation. Do not write files, alter rail state, or create deliverables.

   2. explore 1 (financial-market-analyst 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own only the read-only GOOGL branch. Retrieve GOOGL info and 30-day price history, requested annual income-statement rows, recommendations, and the latest five returned news records. Compute its 30-day change from first and last source observations, preserve dates/values/units, distinguish absent fields from zero, and normalize billions only after retaining raw values. Return history row/date controls, statement years, prices, metrics, recommendation counts, five news records, and validation. Do not query AMZN or write files.

   3. explore 2 (financial-market-analyst 1): Use one explore sub-agent to own only the read-only AMZN branch. Retrieve AMZN info and 30-day price history, compute the change from first and last source observations, preserve dates/values/units, and distinguish absent fields from zero. Return compact history row/date controls, prices, metrics, and validation. Do not query GOOGL, write files, or create deliverables.

   4. explore 3 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to own the read-only meeting-coordination branch. Search the inbox for exact subjects `Q1 2026 Roadshow - Schedule Request` from `investors@fundmanager.com` and `Availability Confirmed - March 10 Meeting` from `shanghai_partners@finance.com`; paginate both result sets, read every candidate, and match by complete sender, recipient, and subject rather than subject alone. Return the exact requested schedule/materials details and the Shanghai partner's stated availability constraint, with message IDs and matching controls. Do not send or modify email.

After Wave 1, the main agent must reconcile units, dates, ticker identity, train feasibility, incoming meeting constraints, and missing fields, then freeze one literal canonical dataset containing every row/slide fact and both outgoing message payloads; the explicit task tickers remain controlling over the conflicting visible configuration. Both artifact writers and the emails consume this exact payload without recomputing stock changes or financial units. The Shanghai meeting time and logistics must honor the partner's source-backed availability and leave a defensible post-arrival transfer buffer; if no returned train makes that possible, report the conflict instead of fabricating a schedule.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/Roadshow_Analysis.xlsx` exclusively. Create Travel_Plan, Stock_Summary, and Financial_Highlights from the canonical payload with the exact required columns, two travel/ticker rows as applicable, at least two GOOGL fiscal years, business class, literal numbers, and correctly converted billion-USD fields. Read back all sheets and return the path, sheet order, row counts, ticker/year controls, and validation. Do not create the presentation or send email.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/Investor_Roadshow.pptx` exclusively. Create the deck exactly once with at least the five required slides, using only the canonical itinerary and finance facts; include both cities, GOOGL financials, GOOGL-versus-AMZN 30-day comparison, and analyst consensus without unsupported claims. Read it back and return path, slide count/titles, ticker coverage, and validation. Do not write the workbook or send email.

After Wave 2, the main agent must cross-check workbook and deck values and then search sent mail for the two exact recipients/contexts, sending at most one missing message to each with verified meeting and deliverable details. It must perform final artifact and message checks before completion.

nodes.text:
CONTEXT: You are supporting a financial analyst preparing an investor roadshow. Gather read-only financial market data for two companies using your Yahoo Finance tools and report findings back in a structured summary. Do not create, modify, or send anything — data gathering and reporting only.

PRIMARY COMPANY — ticker GOOGL (Alphabet Inc.):
1. Call get_stock_info for GOOGL. Report: current/latest share price (with currency), market cap, trailing twelve-month EPS, total revenue (TTM), profit margins if shown, and any analyst recommendation fields (e.g., recommendationKey, numberOfAnalystOpinions, targetMeanPrice).
2. Call get_historical_stock_prices for GOOGL with period="1mo" and interval="1d". Report: the date and closing price of the FIRST trading day in the returned window, the date and closing price of the LAST trading day, and the percent change over the window (=(last close - first close)/first close*100, to 1-2 decimals). Also note the highest and lowest closes in the window.
3. Call get_financial_statement for GOOGL with financial_type="income_stmt" (annual income statement). Report Total Revenue and Net Income for the TWO most recent fiscal years available, with the exact period labels (e.g., 2023, 2024) as returned by the tool. Give both the raw value and the value in billions USD rounded to 2 decimals. Also report diluted EPS for those years if present.
4. Call get_recommendations for GOOGL with recommendation_type="recommendations". Report the strongBuy/buy/hold/sell/strongSell counts and the period/date they refer to, and describe the overall consensus (e.g., "Buy", "Strong Buy").
5. Call get_yahoo_finance_news for GOOGL. Report the latest FIVE news headlines (title, publisher, and link if available).

COMPARISON COMPANY — ticker AMZN (Amazon.com, Inc.):
6. Call get_stock_info for AMZN. Report: current share price, market cap, trailing EPS, total revenue (TTM), and any recommendation fields.
7. Call get_historical_stock_prices for AMZN with period="1mo" and interval="1d". Report: first close (with date), last close (with date), the percent change over the window (to 1-2 decimals), plus the highest and lowest closes in the window.

DELIVERABLE: Return a single structured plain-text report with one section per numbered item (1-7), with exact figures, units, and dates. For any large monetary value, also provide the amount in billions USD rounded to 1-2 decimals. If a field is absent from the tool output, explicitly write "NOT AVAILABLE" for it rather than estimating. Precision matters — this report feeds directly into an Excel workbook and a slide deck that I will build.
Gather GOOGL/AMZN market data

TASK: Build an Excel workbook for an investor roadshow. Create it at EXACTLY this full path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-12306-yf-investor-roadshow-excel-ppt-email/workspace/Roadshow_Analysis.xlsx

Use your mcp__excel__ tools. The workbook must contain exactly three worksheets named exactly: Travel_Plan, Stock_Summary, Financial_Highlights.

HARD RULES:
1. All numeric values must be literal numbers — NO cell may contain a formula (nothing starting with "=").
2. Use the data below EXACTLY as given; do not invent or alter values.
3. Billions figures must have 1-2 decimal places.
4. Header row is row 1 on each sheet; data starts at row 2.

SHEET "Travel_Plan" — headers (row 1, in this exact order):
City, Train_No, Departure, Arrival, Duration_Hours, Class, Ticket_Price_CNY, Meeting_Date
Row 2: Shanghai, G1, 09:00, 13:28, 4.47, Business, 1748.5, 2026-03-10
Row 3: Guangzhou, G105, 08:00, 15:48, 7.8, Business, 2631.5, 2026-03-10
(Departure/Arrival are text times; Duration_Hours is decimal hours: 4h28m = 4.47, 7h48m = 7.8; Ticket_Price_CNY are business-class fares in CNY; Meeting_Date is the text 2026-03-10.)

SHEET "Stock_Summary" — headers (row 1, in this exact order):
Company, Ticker, Current_Price, Change_30D_Pct, Market_Cap_B, Revenue_B, EPS, Recommendation
Row 2: Alphabet Inc., GOOGL, 300.88, -9.17, 3639.75, 402.84, 10.82, Strong Buy
Row 3: Amazon.com Inc., AMZN, 218.94, -1.68, 2350.3, 716.92, 7.18, Strong Buy
(Current_Price in USD; Change_30D_Pct is the ~30-day percent price change, negative allowed; Market_Cap_B and Revenue_B in billions USD; EPS is trailing twelve months.)

SHEET "Financial_Highlights" — headers (row 1, in this exact order):
Metric, Year, Value_B
Row 2: Revenue, 2024, 350.02
Row 3: Revenue, 2025, 402.84
Row 4: Net Income, 2024, 100.12
Row 5: Net Income, 2025, 132.17
(These are Alphabet Inc. annual income statement figures in billions USD; Year as a number.)

STEPS:
1. create_workbook at the path above. If it creates a default sheet (e.g., "Sheet1"/"Sheet"), rename it to "Travel_Plan", then use create_worksheet for "Stock_Summary" and "Financial_Highlights". Ensure no leftover extra/blank sheets remain in the workbook.
2. Use write_data_to_excel for each sheet's data (headers + data rows).
3. Use format_range to bold each header row (row 1) on all three sheets.
4. Verify with read_data_from_excel on each sheet and get_workbook_metadata: confirm the three exact sheet names, all cell values present exactly as specified, and that no cell contains a formula.

DELIVERABLE: Report the final file path, the sheet names found, and confirm every data cell matches the specification above (list any discrepancy). Do not create any other files.
Build Roadshow_Analysis.xlsx workbook

TASK: Build a PowerPoint presentation for an investor roadshow. Create and save it at EXACTLY this full path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-12306-yf-investor-roadshow-excel-ppt-email/workspace/Investor_Roadshow.pptx

Use your mcp__pptx__ tools. Context: an investment firm is presenting Alphabet Inc. (ticker GOOGL) quarterly/full-year results to institutional investors on a two-city roadshow (Shanghai and Guangzhou) on March 10, 2026, traveling from Beijing by high-speed rail (business class). The deck must have 5 slides, in this exact order:

SLIDE 1 — Title slide:
- Main heading MUST reference the investor roadshow and the year 2026, e.g.: "Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) — 2026 Investor Roadshow"
- Subtitle lines: "Quarterly Results Presentation for Institutional Investors"; "City Tour: Beijing → Shanghai → Guangzhou | March 10, 2026"; "Presented by: [Analyst Name], Equity Research"

SLIDE 2 — Title "Travel Itinerary — March 10, 2026":
- Add a table (add_table) with header row: City, Train No., Departure, Arrival, Duration, Seat Class, Price (CNY)
- Data row 1: Shanghai, G1, 09:00 Beijing South, 13:28 Shanghai Hongqiao, 4h 28m, Business, 1748.5
- Data row 2: Guangzhou, G105, 08:00 Beijing South, 15:48 Guangzhou South, 7h 48m, Business, 2631.5
- Below the table add a short note: "Both legs depart Beijing South on March 10, 2026, in business class."

SLIDE 3 — Title "Financial Highlights — Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL)":
Bullets covering revenue growth, net income, and EPS:
- Revenue: $350.02B (FY2024) → $402.84B (FY2025) — +15.1% YoY growth
- Net Income: $100.12B (FY2024) → $132.17B (FY2025) — +32.0% YoY growth
- Diluted EPS: $8.04 (FY2024) → $10.81 (FY2025); trailing EPS $10.82
- Profit margin 32.8% on TTM revenue of $402.84B

SLIDE 4 — Title "30-Day Stock Performance: GOOGL vs AMZN":
- Include a comparison table (add_table), header: Metric, GOOGL, AMZN, with rows:
  Current price, $300.88, $218.94
  30-day change, -9.17%, -1.68%
  Market cap, $3,639.75B, $2,350.30B
  30-day window, 2026-02-05 to 2026-03-05, 2026-02-05 to 2026-03-05
- Add a takeaway bullet: "GOOGL underperformed AMZN over the past month; both declined modestly amid broader technology weakness."
- Optionally also add a simple bar chart of the 30-day change (GOOGL -9.17, AMZN -1.68) if straightforward.

SLIDE 5 — Title "Analyst Consensus & Recommendations — GOOGL":
Bullets:
- Overall consensus: Strong Buy (recommendation mean 1.37; 56 analysts; mean price target $376.86)
- Recommendation breakdown (latest monthly snapshot): Strong Buy 10 | Buy 48 | Hold 7 | Sell 0 | Strong Sell 0
- 58 of 65 ratings at Buy or Strong Buy; price target range $185.00-$443.00
- Peer comparison: AMZN also rated Strong Buy (62 analysts; mean target $280.47)

DESIGN: professional business style (e.g., modern_blue color scheme). Use add_slide with suitable layouts (a title layout for slide 1, title+content for the others), populate title/content placeholders, use add_table for the tables. Use plain ASCII characters (e.g., "-9.17%", "→" is acceptable in subtitle text). Keep text concise so nothing overflows. Save the presentation with save_presentation to the exact path above.

VERIFICATION: After saving, use get_presentation_info and extract_presentation_text to confirm the file has 5 slides and each slide contains its required content (slide 1 heading mentions roadshow and 2026; slide 2 itinerary table has both Shanghai and Guangzhou; slide 3 covers revenue, net income, and EPS; slide 4 compares GOOGL and AMZN 30-day performance; slide 5 summarizes analyst consensus). Report the final path and a slide-by-slide confirmation. Do not create any other files.
Build Investor_Roadshow.pptx deck
